correctness.rationale: For the stated periodic site-space operator the Fourier transform is unitary, and the full norm is the maximum of the block norms. Writing a block as [[0,r],[ell,0]], one obtains ell r=4J² and squared factor norms 4J²(cosh²h∓sinh(h)cos(k)). Hence the cubic identity and the Frobenius trace follow: with u=sinh²h, v=cos²k and s=sin²(Jt), the trace of E*E is 3+8us+4u(u−v)s². Chiral conjugation intertwines E with E inverse, so its three singular values are g,1,1/g and g is the stated increasing function of the trace. For u>0 the time derivative in the variable s is bounded below by 8u min(1,u)>0, and at s=1 the trace decreases strictly in v. The distance of the N-point grid to pi/2 modulo pi is 0, pi/(2N) or pi/N in the three stated cases, including N=2. At h=0 unitarity removes the time and momentum strictness. At fixed h≠0 the derivative with respect to v is finite and strictly negative at v=0, giving the quadratic deficit; at fixed N, Q_N is asymptotic to exp(2|h|)/4, giving the large-bias formula.
residual_risks: Numerical checks sample the formula; the proof establishes all times and momenta. No formal verification or expert attestation.
